description: Machine-readable license registry for every asset the Ezber content pipeline can bundle. The pipeline refuses to build when an asset references a license id that is missing here, when an asset has no attribution, or when a source is on the distribution deny-list. EZBER-LICENSES.json in the build output is this registry enriched with the exact attribution strings of the bundled assets; it is designed to be rendered directly by the app's credits/licenses screen.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported
obligations: Copy and distribute the Quran text verbatim only; changing the text is not allowed.
Clearly indicate the source (Tanzil Project) and link to https://tanzil.net so users can track changes.
Reproduce the Tanzil copyright notice in all verbatim copies of the text and in all files derived from or containing a substantial portion of it (shipped as TANZIL-NOTICE.txt).
licenses.attribution: Quran text (Uthmani, version 1.1): Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net), licensed CC BY 3.0. Served verbatim and unmodified.
licenses.notes: The pipeline fetches the Uthmani XML download and the quran-data.xml metadata; both carry this license and the notice is copied verbatim into the bundle.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
obligations: Credit the recitation/timing distributor (Dhikr Al-Huda App) and the reciter by name.
Link the license (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) and indicate the Internet Archive item the files were obtained from.
The pipeline does not alter the audio or timing files; only checksums and metadata are copied.
licenses.attribution: Recitation audio and ayah timing: {reciter_name} ({qirat}, {style}), provided by Dhikr Al-Huda App on the Internet Archive (item {item_id}), licensed CC BY 4.0.
licenses.notes: Not yet shippable: captain decision CD-2 requires a written confirmation from Quran Foundation before any reciter is enabled, so all current candidates are disabled. Whenever an item is enabled the pipeline machine-checks that it still declares the expected license URL in its Internet Archive metadata.

licenses.name: Tanzil English transliteration - use cleared by written permission

written_permission.scope: Tanzil English transliteration edition en.transliteration, bundled and displayed in the Ezber app
written_permission.record: The written grant is retained in the captain's records and is not committed to this repository. Captain confirmation: 'Tanzil English transliteration is CLEARED by written permission' (inbox 002, 2026-09-25).

obligations: Credit Tanzil Project and link https://tanzil.net in the app credits.
Keep the edition verbatim; the pipeline only strips the page's presentation markup and splits the text into word tokens for display.
Keep the written grant on file alongside the content manifest for store review.
licenses.attribution: Transliteration: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net), used with written permission.
licenses.notes: Source page: https://tanzil.net/trans/en.transliteration (edition en.transliteration, last update September 6, 2010). The page ships the full text with presentation markup; the pipeline strips tags without changing the transliteration letters and verifies the provenance header on every build.

licenses.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (cpfair/quran-align data)
obligations: Credit Collin Fair / cpfair/quran-align and link the repository and the CC BY 4.0 license in the app credits.
State that the pipeline drops or repairs malformed entries from the released timing files and interpolates uncovered words; the manifest records the repair counts per recitation.
licenses.attribution: Word timing data: cpfair/quran-align (https://github.com/cpfair/quran-align), licensed CC BY 4.0.
licenses.notes: The release archive's data files are CC BY 4.0 (the align tool's source code is MIT). The 2016-11-24 release contains 12 recitation files; the Abdurrahmaan As-Sudais file is an align-tool crash log and is excluded, and the remaining 11 files contain a small number of malformed segments that the pipeline repairs deterministically.
